content: This medication is prescribed to treat or prevent bacterial infections. To achieve the best results, it is important to take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using this medication to prevent infections, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Do not skip doses or stop taking the medication without consulting your doctor. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or headache. Taking this medication with food can help reduce nausea. It may also cause your urine to appear dark yellow or brown, which is harmless. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause serious or potentially fatal side effects, such as lung problems, liver disease, blood disorders, or nerve damage. Lung issues may occur within the first month of treatment or after long-term use (typically six months or more). Additionally, it may rarely lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Nitrofurantoin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It should not be used near or at the time of delivery (weeks 38–42 of pregnancy) due to the risk of harm to the newborn, such as a blood disorder called hemolytic anemia. This medication passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on nursing infants younger than one month old or those with a genetic condition called G6PD deficiency. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. While taking this medication, lab tests (such as complete blood counts, kidney and liver function tests, and urine cultures) may be required to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
